Question: Explain the concept of database migrations in Django. How do they differ from database schema migrations? Provide an example of how you would use migrations to add a new field to an existing model.
Answer: Database migrations in Django are a way to manage changes to your database schema. They are a part of the Django ORM (Object-Relational Mapping) and are used to automatically update your database schema to match your models. Migrations are different from schema migrations because they are not just about changing the database schema; they also include the application logic, such as creating, updating, or deleting objects in the database. Migrations are stored in the migrations directory of each app and are applied automatically when you run the migrate command in the Django shell or the command line.

Question: How do you implement authentication in Django? Provide a brief overview of the different authentication backends available in Django and explain when you might choose one over the other. Also, provide an example of how to set up a custom user model in Django.
Answer: Django provides built-in authentication functionality that can be used to create and manage user accounts. The main authentication backends available in Django are the default backend and custom backends. The default backend is the default authentication system that uses the built-in User model. Custom backends allow you to create your own authentication system, which can be useful if you want to use a different database or if you want to add extra functionality to the authentication system. Django also provides a way to create a custom user model, which is useful if you want to add extra fields to the User model.

Question: Describe the process of building a RESTful API in Django. What are the key components of a RESTful API? Provide an example of how to set up a Django REST framework project and a simple API endpoint.
Answer: Building a RESTful API in Django involves several key components, including the Django REST framework, which is a powerful tool for building APIs. The main components of a RESTful API are resources, which are the data that the API exposes, and the HTTP methods used to interact with those resources (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.). The Django REST framework provides a way to define resources and their associated methods, as well as a way to map those resources to URLs.

Question: Explain the concept of code organization in Python. Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of organizing code into modules, packages, and classes. Provide an example of how you would structure a Python project with these concepts in mind.
Answer: Code organization in Python is the process of structuring code in a way that makes it easy to understand, maintain, and extend. There are several ways to organize code in Python, including modules, packages, and classes. Modules are files that contain Python code, and they are used to organize related code into a single file. Packages are directories that contain modules and other packages, and they are used to organize related code into a hierarchical structure. Classes are used to define objects and their behavior, and they are used to encapsulate related data and methods.

Question: How do you write unit tests for a Django application? What are the benefits of writing unit tests? Provide an example of how to write a unit test for a Django view.
Answer: Writing unit tests for a Django application involves testing individual components of the application, such as views, models, and forms. Unit tests are written using the Django test framework, which provides a way to write tests for individual components of the application. The benefits of writing unit tests include ensuring that the application works as expected, making it easier to debug and maintain the application, and providing a way to ensure that the application remains stable and reliable.
